sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Core Demand**: The **Bargadars** (sharecroppers) demanded that the landlord's share be reduced to **1/3rd** (Tebhaga) instead of the traditional **1/2** (Adhi). 
• **Institutional Driver**: Led by the **Bengal Provincial Kisan Sabha (BPKS)**, the movement was a direct response to the **Floud Commission (1940)** recommendations which had suggested the 1/3rd share. 
• **Socio-Economic Context**: Post-WWII inflation, the **Great Bengal Famine (1943)**, and the exploitation by **Jotedars** (rich peasants/intermediaries) created the necessary revolutionary climate. 
• **Key Metric**: The movement was most intense in the northern districts of Bengal, specifically **Dinajpur, Rangpur, and Jalpaiguri**.

items.definition: Sharecroppers who cultivated land owned by Jotedars; they provided labor and inputs but received only half the produce.
A class of rich peasants who emerged as the dominant rural power brokers, often acting as intermediaries between the Zamindars and the actual tillers.
A tactical strategy where peasants stored the harvested paddy in their own barns rather than the landlord's, asserting ownership over the produce.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Floud Commission Implementation**: The movement was essentially a grassroots attempt to force the government to implement the Floud Commission's 1940 report.
• **Women's Participation**: Significant involvement of women (e.g., Rani Bhabani, Ila Mitra) in the 'Nari Bahini' to resist police and landlord repression.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Brutal state repression, communal tensions during the Partition era, and the eventual withdrawal of the movement due to the focus on the Transfer of Power.
• **Legacy**: Laid the groundwork for the **West Bengal Estates Acquisition Act (1953)** and subsequent land reform movements.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'T-R-I-D' (Tebhaga, Rangpur, Ila Mitra, Dinajpur).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Tebhaga movement was centered in Rangpur and Dinajpur, with iconic leadership from figures like Ila Mitra.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Do not confuse Tebhaga with the Indigo Revolt. Tebhaga was a 20th-century movement (1946) focused on sharecropping, not commercial crop production.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Agrarian Radicalism' to describe the shift from the Congress-led peasant movements to the more militant, class-based movements of the 1940s.

keyTakeaways: Tebhaga was a demand for 2/3rd share for the tiller, based on the Floud Commission report.
It marked the peak of the Kisan Sabha's influence in Bengal before the Partition.
The movement demonstrated the power of organized rural mobilization and the active participation of women in anti-feudal struggles.
